PRINCE LEOPOLD GREETS HIS PRINCESS BRIDE ON HER ARRIVAL
ON BELGIAN SOIL, 81126.

Prince Leopold of Belgium greeted his bride, already his Princess by the civil ceremony at Stockholm, with a fond embrace as she stepped from the Swedish cruise Fylgia on to Belgian soil at Antwerp. An address of welcome was read in the town hall before the royal party left for Brussels.
Photo shows. Princess Astrid and the King of the Belgian, on left, Prince Carol (the Brides father) and Prince Leopold, on right, driving through Brussels.

41126.

The favour with which the Belgian people have welcomed Princesss, to her new home is strikingly expressed in these scenes in the Grande Place at Brussels, where from a balcony, the Royal bride watched a thousand children dance in her honour, and where, cheered by a huge gathering of Belgians, she stood for two hours smiling and bowing delightedly.

PRINCESS MARIA JOSE, KING ALBERT'S YOUNG DAUGHTER, RECEIVES HER FIRST COMMUNION. Princess Maria Jose, the only daughter of the King and Queen of the Belgians, received her first communion in the church attached to a refugee which her mother has established in the unoccupied part of the country for children who have been orphaned by the war. The little Princess was ten years old on August 10, 4 her birthday also being the anniversary of the declaration of war. Photo shows. The King talking to the Bishop with the Queen and the Princess.

SHROVE TUESDAY CEREMONY AT THE TOWN OF BINCHE, IN BELGIUM.

On Shrove Tuesday Binche, a little town fifteen miles from Mons, a custom is carried out, dating back from 1540, when a fete was given by Maria of Hungary to celebrate the coquiest of Peru. Townsmen and women, the former wearing the most wondrous plumes, each costing 1,000 francs, sally forth armed with baskets filled with oranges, and unsuspecting visitors are pelted with them. Any persons not wearing carnival dress also come in for the pelting.

TO SAVE THE FIELD OF WATERLOO FROM BUILDERS.

Donations amounting to over £4,000 have been raised in England towards saving the field of Waterloo from being built on. If £10,000 is forthcoming in Great Britain, the Belgian Parliament has passed a bill to acquire the building rights. The Duke of Wellington and Lord Robert are Treasurers of the Fund. Our photo shows the gigantic landmark marking the field of Waterloo.
